changes_data.diff:
@@ -120,6 +120,8 @@ The following features are new (or have been significantly updated) since versio
    “ip.addr != 1.1.1.1” will work as expected (the result is the same as typing “ip.src != 1.1.1.1 and ip.dst != 1.1.1.1”). This avoids the
    contradiction (a == b and a != b) being true.
 ** Use the syntax “a ~= b” or “a any_ne b” to recover the previous (inconsistent with ==) logic for not equal.
+** Set elements must now be separated using a comma (,). A filter such as http.request.method in {"GET" "HEAD"} must be written as ... in {"GET", "HEAD"}.
+   (Whitespace is of course optional.) The previous use of whitespace as separator is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.
 
 * Corrected calculation of mean jitter in RTP Stream Analysis dialog and IAX2 Stram Analysis dialog

commits_data.title: dfilter: Add support for comma as set separator
commits_data.message:
dfilter: Add support for comma as set separator

Deprecate the usage of significant whitespace to separate set elements
(or anywhere else for that matter). This will make the implementation
simpler and cleaner and the language more expressive and user-friendly.

(cherry picked from commit 2183738ef262f4b4937dd9512bdcb3212a4c9fe5)

commits_data.title: dfilter: Fixup deprecated tokens initialization
commits_data.message:
dfilter: Fixup deprecated tokens initialization

Always use the internal API to access "deprecated" and initialize
the data structure on demand. This fixes a potential null pointer
dereference with dfw->deprecated.

Use reference counting to share the array cleanly and avoid memory
leaks.

Keep the pointer in dfwork_t.

(cherry picked from commit 0d3bfedfb0fa3afd3d7787873823b80796097003)
